apps.name: Tasker
apps.comment: The supreme king of Android automation.

apps.name: Key Mapper
apps.comment: Key remappers are super useful for voice and dictation workflows, for instance binding macro pads to dictation apps. Very powerful when used together with MacroDroid and similar apps to fire intents. My usual pattern: Key Mapper does the interception, then Tasker or MacroDroid provides the automation glue.

apps.name: Droid-ify
apps.comment: My favourite F-Droid client. It makes sorting apps by repository easy, which is a great help for propagating updates from private F-Droid repos: my preferred way of sideloading the APKs I build as internal tools.

apps.name: SD Maid SE
apps.comment: One of the few clean-up tools that's actually useful, in my opinion.

apps.name: Tailscale
apps.comment: Essential remote access app.

apps.name: Speedify
apps.comment: A brilliant product to have on hand wherever connectivity is impaired.

apps.name: RCX (rclone)
apps.comment: rclone is just about the best cloud CLI out there; this is a fantastic way to use it on remote devices.

apps.name: FolderSync
apps.comment: One of the few Android apps I've used for many years, maybe even a decade. Vastly useful for all manner of cloud sync operations.

apps.name: ASR Voice Recorder
apps.comment: My go-to voice recorder. I use it constantly, for everything from voice-note prompts for AI tools to podcast episodes. I really appreciate how easy it makes setting up different recording profiles, with precise controls for each use case.

apps.name: Easy Voice Recorder Pro
apps.comment: I do so much voice work that I like to keep a second recorder on hand, and Easy Voice Recorder Pro is also excellent.

apps.name: Spectrum
apps.comment: Having lived in far too many noisy apartments next to building sites and other noise nuisances, I like to keep at least one app on my phone for measuring noise and figuring out which frequencies are coming in. A simple spectrum analysis on an Android phone can often give you a head start on blocking a nuisance sound. This one is reliable and great.

apps.name: phyphox
apps.comment: Absolutely outstanding: it exposes the phone's sensors. I've used it not only to figure out which frequencies were coming in from a noisy construction site, but even to use the gyroscope to work out how much of the sound was travelling as vibration. Mind-blowing that a consumer Android phone can do this.

apps.name: Kokoro TTS
apps.comment: My favourite engine for on-device TTS.

apps.name: SpeakThat
apps.comment: This became indispensable during the protracted war with Iran here in Israel, when we were often woken in the middle of the night by alerts. Having them read out in a calm, sometimes fun voice became a coping mechanism for the stress. Generally useful, and it fits my preference for using voice for just about everything, including receiving notifications.

apps.name: Podcast Addict
apps.comment: The Pro version of Podcast Addict is my go-to podcast client. Very happy with it.

apps.name: Timestamp Camera
apps.comment: Extremely versatile and useful in so many situations: evidence for tenancy and landlord issues, templates for recording inventory, labelling network gear during tests, photographing PCBs when opening up components.

apps.name: Genius Scan
apps.comment: My favourite scanning tool, and a cornerstone of my lifelong effort to minimise paper and digitise whatever possible. A well thought-out app with quick workflows and shortcuts for sending scans to repeatable targets.

apps.name: ProofMode
apps.comment: Another great app to have on your phone if you need to document photographs for legal or other reasons.

apps.name: ImageMeter
apps.comment: One of my all-time favourite apps, and one of the few I've carried across devices over the years. Unbelievably useful for anyone renovating or measuring up a place. I highly recommend the Pro plan.

apps.name: Binary Eye
apps.comment: I always keep a QR code scanner as part of my home inventory system, and this is the one I like best.

apps.name: Nuclino
apps.comment: Huge fan of their approach to keeping notes simple. They had the best out-of-the-box Markdown handling before everyone started adding it for its usefulness as AI context.

apps.name: Inoreader
apps.comment: Key tooling for staying informed, especially living in a volatile part of the world.

apps.name: Pushover
